claimUnits.candidateClaim: A cooperative maneuver is admitted only after evaluating the planner output produced with the observed cooperative messages.
claimUnits.functionalTest: Check whether prior work already evaluates a proposed driving action before execution and rejects it in favor of a fallback when a separate criterion fails, regardless of whether that criterion is called a shield, monitor, counterfactual evaluation, or runtime assurance check.
claimUnits.finding: Functionally occupied. Counterfactual policy evaluation for autonomous driving already gates execution after evaluating counterfactual worlds, and runtime-assurance and shielding work already rejects a primary action and switches to a fallback. Binding the gate to V2X message use changes the trigger and evidence channel, not the admission architecture.
claimUnits.classification: known mechanism configured for cooperative-message admission
claimUnits.residualDifference: The proposed gate is membership-conditioned and compares cooperative-message use to message masking, which the located driving shields do not explicitly report.

claimUnits.candidateClaim: The set of tracked road users outside the V2X coalition is defined before either planner branch and held fixed across the comparison.
claimUnits.functionalTest: Check whether prior work distinguishes coalition members from outsiders or non-deviators and evaluates externalities on that fixed complement, rather than merely including all nearby actors in a welfare or safety objective.
claimUnits.finding: Coalitional-game work has long represented payoffs and externalities for outsiders and non-deviators. Driving work routinely evaluates neighboring HDVs and traffic-flow effects, but no located primary source fixes the complement of a message-defined V2X coalition as the estimand population across paired planner branches. Freezing the set is nevertheless causal design hygiene against post-treatment selection, not by itself a new control algorithm.
claimUnits.classification: potentially distinct estimand population, not a new mechanism
claimUnits.residualDifference: A pre-treatment, message-membership-conditioned outsider population in cooperative driving was not found in the verified corpus.

claimUnits.candidateClaim: At the same physical state, planner, prediction horizon, and random seed, the cooperative branch is compared with a branch in which peer cooperative messages are masked and the ego-only fallback is enabled.
claimUnits.functionalTest: Check for baseline-relative side-effect measures, safe-policy counterfactual harm constraints, same-situation counterfactual driving evaluation, and message or information ablations that estimate the incremental effect of cooperation.
claimUnits.finding: The general causal object is occupied. Prior work decomposes side-effect control into a baseline policy or state plus a deviation measure, directly constrains harm relative to an alternate safe policy, and performs pre-execution counterfactual evaluation in autonomous driving. Message masking supplies a domain-specific intervention and may define a useful new cooperative-driving estimand, but it does not create a new class of counterfactual method.
claimUnits.classification: known baseline-relative counterfactual with a V2X-specific intervention
claimUnits.residualDifference: The verified papers do not use peer-message masking to isolate coalition-enabled spillover onto a frozen outsider set.

claimUnits.candidateClaim: The cooperative branch is vetoed when predicted worst-outsider burden exceeds the fallback branch, with outsider non-regression preceding participant gain and no tuned scalar tradeoff.
claimUnits.functionalTest: Check for do-no-harm constraints relative to a baseline, Pareto or no-worse-off admission rules, lexicographic planning constraints, minimum-disruption constraints, and backup-controller switching.
claimUnits.finding: Functionally occupied in its current scalar form. Baseline-relative do-no-harm constraints, Pareto no-worse-off reasoning, lexicographic motion-planning constraints, minimum-disruption cooperative lane-change controllers, and runtime fallback switching all predate the candidate. The max-over-outsiders endpoint is also not actor-wise non-regression: one outsider can be made worse while another improves enough to reduce the maximum.
claimUnits.classification: known do-no-harm or Pareto-style guard applied to a membership-conditioned burden metric
claimUnits.residualDifference: Only the choice to prioritize a V2X-defined outsider burden over coalition utility is specific; the veto logic is not.

searchAudit.candidateScope: Functional novelty of coalition-outsider-counterfactual-veto only; no scoring, acceptance-threshold inference, or idea-center synthesis.
searchAudit.evaluationRule: Terms were not treated as evidence of equivalence or difference. A collision was recorded when a source implements the same causal or control function under different vocabulary. A difference was retained only when it changes the estimand, admissible action set, guarantee, or information intervention.
searchAudit.sourcePolicy: Verified references are primary paper pages, arXiv records, proceedings pages, or publisher pages. Search snippets were used for discovery only; functional findings were checked against source abstracts, accessible full text, or publisher-provided article summaries.

limitations: No located source used the exact four-part composition of a message-defined coalition, a pre-branch frozen outsider set, peer-message masking, and a burden-first admission rule.
Absence of that exact composition is not evidence that each component or the composed controller is a new method; the verified corpus supplies direct functional priors for every component.
Publisher pages that denied full-text access were used only where the publisher-provided abstract, highlights, or an official open manuscript exposed the relevant objective and constraints.
The audit establishes literature novelty, not validity of the proposed simulator identification assumptions or empirical occurrence of outsider harm.

verifiedReferences.title: Socially Compatible Control Design of Automated Vehicle in Mixed Traffic
verifiedReferences.verifiedFunctionalContent: Optimizes AV reward together with courtesy to the following human driver's original plan and reports reduced disruption to that plan.
verifiedReferences.relationToCandidate: Directly occupies outsider-aware courtesy in mixed traffic, but uses a weighted social objective rather than a message-masked paired veto.

verifiedReferences.title: A Cooperative Optimal Control Framework for Connected and Automated Vehicles in Mixed Traffic Using Social Value Orientation
verifiedReferences.venue: IEEE Conference on Decision and Control
verifiedReferences.verifiedFunctionalContent: Combines egoistic and cooperative objectives through SVO and an exact-potential-game control formulation for CAV-HDV merging.
verifiedReferences.relationToCandidate: Strong all-participant social-control baseline; lacks a fixed nonmember complement and fallback-relative harm constraint.

verifiedReferences.title: Cooperative energy and time-optimal lane change maneuvers with minimal highway traffic disruption
verifiedReferences.verifiedFunctionalContent: Selects cooperating vehicles and explicitly limits traffic-flow disruption, with a maximal allowable disruption and time relaxation when infeasible.

verifiedReferences.verifiedFunctionalContent: Builds system utility from participant utilities, uses Shapley marginal contributions, and adapts HDV preferences; its participant set changes as vehicles enter or leave the bottleneck.
verifiedReferences.relationToCandidate: Direct adaptive potential-game and Shapley baseline. It protects modeled participants, not a pre-branch frozen set of message-defined nonmembers.

verifiedReferences.verifiedFunctionalContent: Formulates a control constraint on counterfactual harm of a learned policy relative to an alternate safe policy.
verifiedReferences.relationToCandidate: Strongest mechanism collision: the candidate's fallback-relative non-regression is a driving and subgroup-specific instance of this baseline-relative harm constraint.

verifiedReferences.verifiedFunctionalContent: Defines coalition-structure formation with intra- and inter-coalition externalities and partition-specific payoffs for every player.

strongestObjection.statement: The candidate factors into already known functions: counterfactual pre-execution policy evaluation, harm relative to an alternate safe policy, runtime fallback switching, lexicographic or hard-constraint prioritization, minimum-disruption cooperative driving, and coalition externality accounting. Freezing a V2X-defined nonparticipant set and masking peer messages can define a previously unreported subgroup causal contrast, but that is an estimand and audit protocol, not an irreducible new method.
strongestObjection.additionalDefect: The stated max-over-outsiders veto does not guarantee non-regression for each outsider. Harm can move from the previous worst-off actor to another actor while the maximum decreases. Calling this a nonparticipant non-regression veto overstates the guarantee unless the comparison is actor-wise or the claim is renamed as worst-burden non-regression.
strongestObjection.methodCategory: known counterfactual do-no-harm and runtime-assurance mechanism transferred to cooperative driving
strongestObjection.estimandCategory: potentially new membership-conditioned outsider spillover estimand
strongestObjection.notSupportedCategory: new general control method or new all-actor safety principle

requiredChanges.change: Reframe the work as a V2X-membership-conditioned externality estimand and audit protocol. Do not claim novelty for counterfactual admission, do-no-harm constraints, lexicographic vetoes, or fallback switching.

Choose one defensible guarantee: enforce actor-wise burden non-regression on the frozen set, define a lexicographically sorted burden vector, or rename the rule as worst-outsider aggregate non-regression. The current max statistic cannot support an every-outsider claim.

Specify the structural intervention represented by message masking. Hold initial state, planner, prediction model, horizon, stochastic draws, and pre-treatment actor set fixed; document which participant actions are allowed to change and why the masked branch is a valid ego-only fallback rather than an out-of-distribution planner failure.

Do not describe the method as threshold-free without qualification. The zero contrast is untuned, but actor-envelope radius, horizon, burden definition, prediction model, feasibility tolerances, and any uncertainty margin remain consequential design thresholds.

Include direct functional baselines for Vaskov et al.'s alternate-safe-policy harm constraint, Hart and Knoll's pre-execution counterfactual evaluation, minimally disruptive lane changing, Automatica 111651, all-neighbor safety, SVO/social compatibility, APG/Shapley control, and a standard runtime-assurance fallback.

Show episodes where all-actor collision safety and minimum-disruption baselines admit the cooperative action but the membership-conditioned rule rejects it, and where the difference cannot be reproduced by changing an SVO or social-welfare weight. Otherwise the proposed layer is behaviorally redundant.

Treat a positive result as an empirical contribution only if naturally occurring or public scenarios show a repeatable participant-gain and excluded-actor-burden sign reversal under paired episode analysis, across at least two justified response-model cohorts, with sensitivity to actor envelope, horizon, and burden endpoint. An injected sign reversal is not sufficient.

A null or negative result is independently useful only if equivalence bounds exclude a deployment-relevant outsider burden over broad, preregistered scenario coverage and thereby justify removing the extra admission layer. Failure to find harm in a small simulator sweep is neither a novelty contribution nor a consequential negative result.

State explicitly that even a strong positive finding would validate the new estimand, not retroactively make the veto mechanism novel. Conversely, if existing minimum-disruption or social-control baselines dominate on the same paired contrast, retire the method claim.
